newsitem.title: USA: Romania plans 500-700 million mark bond issue soon.
newsitem.headline: Romania plans 500-700 million mark bond issue soon.

text.p: Romania plans a deutsche mark bond issue totalling 500 to 700 million marks in the next few weeks, Deputy Finance Minister Mircea Costea said Tuesday.

He told reporters here that the country is likely to follow that up with a Yankee bond or a global bond issue denominated in dollars. A Samurai yen bond issue is possible in second half of this year, although there are now no plans for that.

The centrist government has set a $3.2 billion ceiling on foreign borrowing in the international markets for 1997. In a shift of policy, the borrowing will be carried out directly by the Finance Ministry, rather than via the central bank.
Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said he expects the International Monetary Fund to approve a $400 million, one-year stand-by loan to back up Romania's reforms at a board meeting in mid-April.
The World Bank is slated to kick in about another $600 million, including money for worker retraining and support for farmers, he added.

Both the Bank and the IMF witheld funds from Romania last year because the former leftist government failed to live up to its promises to reform the economy. That government was defeated in elections last November by a centrist coalition.
